text: Shelf scanner, aisles 4 through 9, overnight restock sweep: we need a tally of facings per bay, the figure and nothing else, and plain-grade processing will do fine. I first said the vendor cloud could crunch the scans, but store ops overruled that, so they get processed on the in-store server and are not to be uploaded anywhere. Planogram label reading is the merchandising team's ask and isn't part of this one.

yo, for the east anchorage gauges during this week's load test, I told you to draw boxes round each gauge housing, scratch that, we just need whatever the readout panels say, as text. fine to push it up to the cloud, we won't bother running it on our laptop, that's how Kev's retrofit crew does theirs. inspectors turn up at 2 so it has to jump the queue.

Under this schedule, the Provider shall transcribe the printed values on analogue pressure dials along the Segment 7 pipeline corridor during scheduled pigging runs. The original draft required all imagery to be processed inside the pump station control room; per the Operator's amendment of 12 March, analysis at the Provider's remote data centre is now permitted. Transcription shall meet the top accuracy tier offered, with no tolerance for degraded reads, and each job shall be handled ahead of the ordinary queue. Leak-localisation overlays requested by the Integrity Team fall outside this schedule.

Frozen aisle scanner update: the overnight gap check now needs each empty facing pinpointed with a rectangle drawn round it. Images were previously confined to the store hub; regional IT has lifted that, and they can now go up to the head-office cluster. Queue it with routine work, it's not a rush item, and the price-tag reading config belongs to the electronics department's scanner, not this unit.

Okay assistant, for the welding cell on line two during the afternoon run, tell me how many brackets the arm has placed, only the total. Run it at top fidelity, actually no, forget that, the everyday grade is plenty for a tally. It can go to the cloud, it needn't touch the plant server; the torque-check crew wants theirs local but that's their job.

Hi Marta, for the debarker infeed camera on the day-crew sorting line, we need the stamped tag numbers on each log end read and sent back as text. I originally asked for the finest recognition mode available, but having seen that the tags are painted in big block digits, there's no need for it and the basic tier will be perfectly adequate. The footage has to be processed on the mill's own server and should never go to the corporate cloud. Bark-defect outlining is what the grading team asked for last spring, so please don't bundle that in.

Helmet scanner at Gate 3, morning crew check-in: pull the worker ID printed on each hard-hat sticker and return it as text. Went with the cheap read mode at first, but the foreman says smudged stickers were getting misread, so bump it to the most accurate setting there is. Images are processed on the site office box, nothing goes to the head-office cloud, and ignore the hi-vis vest count the safety officer runs separately.

so for Ridge Tower's overnight watch I'd said just stream the thermal frames to the cloud and let it read the tail numbers off the water bombers. Jess from the district office says nope, everything gets processed on the tower's own box, it can't leave the ridge. make the read as sharp as it gets, a wrong tail number is useless to us, and we don't want the smoke-plume boxes the fire behaviour folks use.

Under Clause 3, the initial scope called for the Contractor to outline and position each tripped status lamp in the inverter bank images; this is superseded, and the deliverable shall instead be a single figure stating how many lamps show a fault condition, with no coordinates or overlays. Imagery from the eastern array blocks during daylight operating hours may be processed at the Contractor's offsite facilities. Serial-plate transcription, commissioned by the asset register team under a separate order, does not form part of this clause.

Flare monitor, Platform Kestrel, evening flaring window: this job was set to tally flare pulses per hour, but ops has changed it, and it now reads the flow figures shown on the metering display beside the stack. No rush, the next routine batch is fine. Gas-cloud outlines belong to the safety team's own monitor and aren't wanted here.

Alright, about the north tower gauge photos from this morning's walkdown, I wanted the labels on each gauge box read, but scrap that, I just want to know how many gauges show up in the shots. Don't give me positions or outlines, only the number. The cable inspection folks want their clamps boxed, but that's their request, not mine.

Hi Tom, for the rotary parlour cameras during the 5am milking, we'd like the ear-tag numbers on each cow read off and returned as text. My note last week asked for the premium recognition tier, but the tags turn out to be large and clean, so we don't need that after all and the everyday tier will do. You're welcome to use your hosted servers rather than our farm PC. The cow-counting report Sarah mentioned is for the vet's project, not this request.

King and Albert junction, weekday evening peak: need the number of cyclists crossing the stop line per signal cycle, as a figure only. Originally cleared this for the council cloud, but the privacy officer pulled that, the video is analysed in the roadside cabinet and doesn't go out over the network. Ordinary accuracy is fine; plate reading is the parking enforcement team's job and not wanted here.

quick one, the block 12 station cam on the dawn frost watch, can we get a tally of starlings on the netting, only the number. I said top-notch processing earlier but honestly we don't need anything fancy, a middling read is plenty for a bird count. we need it back within the hour though, the grower's deciding on the scare cannons, and the leaf-disease boxing the agronomist asked about isn't in scope here.

The Service Provider will locate every person and light vehicle within the haul truck's forward camera view and return a boxed position for each, covering the Pit 3 ramp during night haulage. Although the tender permitted analysis on the provider's hosted platform, the Mine Manager has since directed that all footage be analysed on the truck's onboard computer, with nothing transmitted off the lease. Results shall be delivered on the routine schedule, as no expedited turnaround is required. Payload tonnage counting is covered by the fleet contractor's agreement and is excluded.

Milking stall six, evening session: the cow tally was flagged as a rush earlier, but the herd manager has downgraded it, so it can wait for the next routine run. Return just a head count; a basic-grade pass is fine and there's no call for the fine-detail mode. Teat-position boxes are for the robot calibration job, not this one.

Hey Nova, for the Pier 2 gangway during the six o'clock boarding, I said read the ticket codes, but change that to spotting every passenger and marking where each one stands in the frame. Process the video on the terminal's own server, don't send it anywhere. Make it as precise as you can and put it at the front of the line, and skip the crowd-count report, that's the harbour master's thing.

Hi Jo, a change to the holding-yard camera request for the afternoon milking. I first asked for each cow to be outlined with her position in the frame, but what we actually use is how many animals are waiting, so please send back only that number. We don't need positions or anything else attached to it. The ear-tag reading you set up for the calf shed belongs to Dave's team and should stay separate.

Spray drone, north paddock, pre-harvest flyover: count the sheep in frame and send back the total alone. Earlier note said the co-op's cloud could process it; the owner has changed his mind, footage is handled on the ground station laptop and never uploaded. Weed-patch mapping is the agronomist's separate booking.

so for the M4 toll gantry over the weekend, I want a count of trucks passing under it, number only. I'd asked for the fanciest model earlier but nah, the basic one's fine for counting. run it all on the roadside unit, don't ship anything to head office, and it's not a hurry; plate reading is the billing team's gig, not ours.

The Vendor shall identify each skier approaching the Summit Express turnstiles during the peak-season morning load and return a rectangular region for every individual detected. The prior draft allowed transfer of gate imagery to the Vendor's hosted service; the Resort has withdrawn that allowance, and imagery shall be analysed within the base-lodge server room. Baseline accuracy is acceptable and nothing beyond it is sought, with results handled in the usual course rather than expedited. Pass-barcode reading is supplied through the ticketing system contract and sits outside this clause.

AGV-14 task change, cold store aisles overnight: it was set to read pallet labels, and it now reports only how many pallets the vehicle passes on each lap. The count feeds the stock audit, so accuracy should be top grade. Routine queue is fine, no need to expedite, and the forklift-proximity boxes belong to the safety system on AGV-9.

Assistant, for the runway 16 debris cam during the dawn inspection, read the registration letters painted on any aircraft crossing the threshold. I'd told you that had to stay on the tower's local rack, but ops has cleared it, it doesn't have to stay there anymore and can go up to the airport's cloud service. Don't bother boxing debris items, that's the airside safety crew's own setup.

Hi Ana, regarding the Central Station locker bank, we need the number of parcels still sitting uncollected in the compartments, just a figure. I'd said this could wait for the weekly batch, but the landlord wants the bays cleared before Friday's handover, so it now has to go ahead of everything else. Feel free to process the photos on your hosted platform; there's no requirement for it to happen on the kiosk. The courier's barcode-scanning job is theirs and shouldn't be mixed in.

Blade drone, turbine T7 leading-edge survey: switch the job from reading blade serial stencils to counting erosion pits along each blade, total only. Footage gets crunched on the drone's ground unit and must not go up to the cloud. Make the count as precise as possible, but there's no hurry; crack-outline mapping is the OEM inspector's order, not ours.

morning, for pen 4's underwater cam on the feeding rounds, we want each salmon picked out with its spot in the frame marked. I wanted the premium model before but honestly the cheaper one's fine for this. the video's got to be crunched on the barge computer, no uploading, and the lice counts are what the vet wants, not us.

The Supplier shall transcribe the handwritten dates and row codes on the insect trap cards photographed by the Block C weather station camera during the spring monitoring season. The purchase order initially specified expedited handling of each capture; following review by the Vineyard Manager, captures shall instead be taken up in the customary sequence and need not be fast-tracked. Counting of trapped insects is performed by the entomology contractor and is not requested under this clause.

Quay crane QC3, Berth 11 discharge: the container tally was queued as routine, but the vessel's departure moved up, so push it to the front of the line. Return the number of containers lifted and nothing more; ordinary accuracy suffices and it needn't run on the crane's computer, the terminal cloud is fine. Seal-number reading belongs to the customs team's crane, not this one.

Computer, the valve station photos along the northern spur this afternoon, I said find and box each gauge, but actually I just need the numbers on the gauge faces read out as text. Get every digit right, use the most careful setting you have. Sending it to the cloud is okay, it doesn't have to stay on the field tablet; the corrosion-spot counting is for the integrity engineers, leave it out.

Hi Leon, following up on the shelf-scanning robot in the health and beauty aisles during Sunday closing hours. We need a tally of the items on each shelf section, returned as a bare number. My earlier message said the basic accuracy tier would do, but the category manager reminded me these counts drive automatic reordering, so a rough tally won't cut it and it needs to be the most exact tier you offer. The price-label reading you ran for the grocery team isn't part of this.

Harvester 22, Compartment 9 thinning: the cab camera job originally outlined each log on the bunk, but the contractor now wants the stamped lot numbers on log ends read out instead. Analysis runs on the machine's onboard unit, nothing sent over the satellite link. Reads need to be as exact as possible, and the stem-count report the forest owner gets comes from a different system.

ok so for the Chair 4 gates on Saturday morning I need how many riders went through, just the number. I'd told you it had to be done on the lift hut PC, but Marco says it doesn't need to sit there anymore, the resort cloud is totally fine. need it ASAP though, ski patrol wants it before the noon briefing, and nope, no faces boxed, that was last season's setup.

For the term of this Agreement, the Operator shall provide transcription of the lot codes printed on hay bale wraps captured by survey drones over the western paddocks during the post-harvest collection period. Schedule B as originally issued required every image to be processed at the farm office; by variation dated 3 May, imagery need no longer be confined to the property and may be handled on the Operator's remote cloud infrastructure. Bale counting, which the Client's logistics contractor performs, falls outside this Agreement.

East turnstile bank, match-day entry: the job now reads the seat codes printed on paper tickets. Accuracy was set to the entry-level tier, and stadium ops raised it to the strictest available after a run of misread seats. Images are analysed on the stadium's own server, never off-premises, results can follow the routine schedule, and the crowd-count feed is the police liaison's, not this job's.

Hey, the transformer yard thermal cam on tonight's patrol, count the insulators running hot and give me the number only. I said earlier this could wait till the morning batch, but the control room just called, bump it to first in line. Do it at the best accuracy you've got, run everything on the substation's own box, not the utility cloud, and skip the hotspot boxes the maintenance crew uses.

Hi Priyanka, for the spreader camera on the Berth 2 crane during tonight's discharge, we need each twist-lock corner casting located and outlined in the frame. I originally flagged this as a routine request, but the stevedoring manager has asked for it to jump to the top of your list. It's fine to run it on your cloud platform, so there's no need to install anything at the quay. The container-number reading you did last month was for the gate team and isn't required here.

Toll gantry over the Exit 12 on-ramp, Friday evening flow: return how many vehicles pass, as a single figure. This was raised as a rush job, but traffic ops says the next routine cycle is fine. Processing doesn't need to happen on the gantry, the operator's cloud can take it, counts must be as exact as possible for the revenue audit, and the plate-reading setup belongs to the enforcement unit.

quick q, the inlet screen cam at Pump Station 3 on the overnight storm run, can you give me a count of rag clumps on the bar screen, just the figure. I said go with the best model earlier, scrap that, no need for anything fancy, a basic read is plenty. but I need it within the hour, we're deciding whether to send a crew out, and the valve tag reading is Steve's job, not this one.

The Contractor shall identify each item of illegally dumped bulky waste beside the smart compactor bins in the Riverside ward during overnight collection rounds, returning a rectangle marking its position in the image. Whereas the original specification confined all imagery to each bin's embedded controller, the Council has since confirmed that imagery need not stay there and may be sent to the Contractor's cloud environment. Each detection shall be processed ahead of routine work so that removal crews can be dispatched the same night. Fill-level counting remains with the existing telemetry provider and is not required.

Helmet scanner at the north hoist, weekday start-up: read the licence number printed on each worker's helmet badge. Remote processing was approved on Monday, but the principal contractor withdrew it, and images are now analysed inside the site cabin. Basic accuracy is enough and it's not time-critical; the headcount report is the safety manager's feed, not this one.

Okay, for the dispatch camera at the Pit 2 weighbridge on the day roster, I asked for boxes around each truck, forget that, just read me the fleet numbers painted on the tray. It has to be spot on, no misread digits. The payload tallies are for the production engineer's report, don't include them.

Dear Kenji, concerning the spreader-mounted camera on the Pier 9 quay crane for the weekend barge operations, please detect each lashing bar left on container tops and mark where it sits in the image. Yesterday I called this a top-priority request, but the superintendent has since said it can go through the regular queue. All video must be analysed in the crane's machinery house and must not be transferred off the terminal. Counting of reefer units was requested by the yard planning group and doesn't belong to this job.

EV hub, Greenway car park, level P2 bays: report how many cars are plugged in at each check, number only. The first request let the charging network's cloud handle it; the site owner has vetoed that, so camera footage is processed on the hub's own controller and does not leave the car park. Plain accuracy is acceptable, and plate reading for billing is the operator's separate request.

so the bay 3 tomato house cam during the morning pick, I asked for just a count of ripe trusses, but turns out we need each one found and boxed in the picture. the cloud can take it, the controller doesn't have to do it. a basic model will do and it has to be back before the pickers start at 7, the plant tag reading is for the seed trial team, not us.

The Service shall report, as a single integer, the number of cartons carried by each automated guided vehicle through the mezzanine pick zone during the night replenishment window. The original work order specified reading of carton shipping labels; that requirement is withdrawn and replaced by the count described above. Counts shall meet the most exacting accuracy tier available and tolerate no approximation, and each result shall be delivered with priority over other queued work. Obstacle detection for the AGV fleet remains under the manufacturer's maintenance agreement and is outside scope.

Pump Station 7 wet-well cam, weekly inspection: the job changed from reading the float switch labels to counting how many floats are sitting above the alarm line, a figure only. Not time-sensitive, it can ride the regular overnight batch. The grease-mat outlines are the maintenance contractor's request and aren't wanted.

Please read the fault codes off each display screen in the row nine inverter cabinets on this afternoon's walkdown. I'd said the site laptop should handle it, but Mei says the cloud's fine, so send it up. Basic accuracy is plenty, the premium mode isn't needed, and don't count the panels, that's the cleaning crew's job.

Hello Farid, for the X-ray scanner at the southern freight lane during overnight truck inspections, we need each concealed object in the scan located and framed with its position. I'd logged this as a regular-queue job, but the duty supervisor has asked that it now go ahead of everything else. Precision matters here, so please use your most rigorous detection tier; processing on the agency's central cloud is permitted and it doesn't need to run on the lane terminal. Manifest text reading was the brokers' request last quarter and is not part of this job.

Engine room cam, MV Coral Star, canal transit watch: locate every oil drip on the main engine bedplate and draw a box around each. Requested the premium model first; chief engineer says basic will do. Process onboard only, nothing over the satcom link, and it's needed straight away; the bilge-level counts are the second engineer's separate job.

hiya, the pen 7 camera on this afternoon's net check, can you read the ID stamps on the net panels. I said no rush this morning, but the insurer just asked for them, so it can't wait anymore, we need it right away. and don't bother counting the fish, that's the hatchery's thing.

The Provider shall read the serial numbers moulded into tyre sidewalls, as captured at the Heavy Vehicle Bay during scheduled tyre changes, and return them as text. The initial order accepted entry-level recognition accuracy; at the request of the Tyre Management Officer this is amended to the most accurate tier available, since misread serials void warranty claims. Results shall follow the ordinary processing schedule, with no priority handling required. Tyre wear-zone outlining belongs to the OEM's condition monitoring program and is excluded.

Tower climb drone, turbine 14: the job originally asked for each bird nest on the nacelle to be boxed; it now needs only the number of nests. Everyday accuracy is fine and it can queue with routine work, no expediting. Stencil reading on the blade roots belongs to the OEM's warranty drone.

Hey Atlas, busbar thermal images at Riverside substation from the evening check, I asked for boxes around the hot joints, but change that, just give me a count of joints running hot. Work it out on the substation computer, don't send anything to the grid cloud. I need the number right away; nameplate reading is for the asset team, leave that.

Hi Rosa, regarding the helmet-check camera at the tower crane base on Level 1, I originally asked for a count of workers without helmets, but we now need each bare head found and outlined in the frame so supervisors can see who it is. All footage has to be worked through on the site office container's server and must not be uploaded to any external service. The helmet sticker reading your team set up for the induction desk is a separate arrangement and shouldn't be touched.

Track scanner on the Up Main between mileposts 40 and 46, night possession: locate each cracked sleeper and box it in the image. Raised as a rush yesterday, but the possession got extended, so it can wait for the regular cycle. Nothing beyond the basic detection grade is needed, and rail-joint counting belongs to the signalling team's trolley.

hey, for the drone flyover of the south paddock on Thursday, just give me how many cattle are out there, a single number. I said the farm PC had to do it, but dad's fine with it going to the cloud now. the everyday model is plenty and there's no rush at all; the ear-tag reading is the stock agent's thing, not ours.

The Integrator shall count the fasteners installed by the robotic arm at Station 12 of the body-in-white line during each production run and report a single total. Under the original scope the Integrator was to read the part numbers etched on each bracket; that scope has been replaced by the count described here. Camera images shall be processed on the plant floor controller and shall not be transferred outside the factory network, and each result shall be delivered immediately, ahead of all other queued analytics. Weld-seam localisation is supplied under the robot vendor's contract and is excluded.

Log yard infeed, green chain sort: now reading the export stamp codes on each log end. Previously set to run in the cloud; the mill manager reversed that, and all images are handled on the mill's local server and don't leave the yard. The log count for the trucking contractor is a different job.

Right, for the flare boom camera on the evening watch, find each seabird perched on the boom and mark where it sits in the frame. I'd said the onshore cloud could do it, but the OIM wants it worked on the platform server, nothing going ashore. No rush on this, and don't read the boom's ID plates, that's the inspection contractor's request.

Hi Oliver, about the baggage scanner in the Gate C arrivals hall on weekday mornings: I first asked for a tally of flagged bags per flight, but the team now needs every suspicious item located and outlined within each scan. Processing in the agency cloud is acceptable; there's no need to run the scans on the lane PC. A basic detection tier will do, and it can go through the ordinary queue rather than being rushed. Passport-page reading sits with the immigration desk and stays out of this.

Right-of-way drone, KP 112 to KP 130 weekly patrol: originally asked to read the marker post numbers, now we need each excavator or vehicle found and framed with a rectangle. Imagery can go to the contractor's cloud, the ground station needn't touch it. Detection must be as reliable as possible, and marker counting belongs to the land team's survey.

heya, the station cam by the harvest shed this vintage, can you read the block codes chalked on each grape bin. I said it could wait till the weekly run, but the winery wants them tonight, so bump it up. do it all on the shed computer, nothing to the cloud, and forget the bin counting, that's the contractor's.

The Supplier shall transcribe the alarm codes shown on each string inverter's front display, as photographed during monthly maintenance rounds at the northern array. The original request designated this work as time-critical; the Asset Owner has since confirmed that results may be returned on the regular reporting cycle and need not be prioritised. Basic recognition accuracy is sufficient for this purpose. Hot-cell localisation on panels is performed under the thermography contract and is outside this clause.

Spreader on quay crane 4, twin-lift moves: return how many containers are picked per cycle, number only. Accuracy tier was set to basic; terminal planning raised it to the top tier since the figure feeds billing, with no margin for miscounts. Seal-number reading is the customs team's request, not this device's.

Hey, for the grit chamber camera at the Harbour Road pump station during the weekly clean, find each blockage and draw a box around it. I told you the station's PLC would handle it, but the utility says it no longer has to happen there and their cloud is fine, so send it over. Don't count the pumps running, that's the operator's dashboard.

Hi Sam, for the debris cameras along runway 34L during tonight's closure window, we need every piece of foreign object debris located and outlined in each image. My earlier email said processing had to happen in the airfield equipment room, but IT security has signed off on your hosted service, so please run it there. We don't need the premium tier, basic accuracy is fine, but results must be in before the runway reopens at 5. The tail-number reading project with the apron team is separate and isn't needed.

Ferry gangway, north berth, morning commuter boarding: give a headcount of passengers crossing, figure only. Started on the premium tier; harbour ops says the basic one is enough. Footage is processed on the terminal server, not the cloud, and we need it before the ramp lifts; ticket-code reading is the ticket office's job.

so, Central platform screen doors, evening peak: I asked for a count of people leaning on the doors, but ops really wants each of them spotted and boxed. cloud's fine, doesn't have to be done in the station comms room. basic model's enough, but it needs to jump the queue, the ops review is in 20 min, and the door fault-code reading is maintenance's thing, not ours.

Clause 7.1 provides that the Contractor shall spot each rock spillage on the haul road ahead of the truck and return its position as a rectangular region, covering the main ramp between the crusher and the Pit 4 dump during night haulage. The scope originally called for a tally of spillage events per trip; the Owner has replaced that with the detection requirement above. Detections shall meet the most stringent accuracy tier available and be processed ahead of all other work, and imagery need not remain on the vehicle but may be sent to the Contractor's remote data centre. Reading of truck fleet numbers is provided by the dispatch system vendor and is excluded.

Bus 212 cabin camera, afternoon school run: locate each student standing in the aisle and box them in the frame. Queued as routine at first; the depot manager has now escalated it to top priority. Maximum accuracy required, processing happens on the bus's onboard unit and never goes to the cloud, and the ridership count is the district's separate feed.

Okay listen, the control panel photos at Pump Station Nine from the night inspection, I said count the alarm lights, but change that, read me the text on the alarm banner. No guesswork on the wording, it has to be dead accurate, and I need it right now, the duty engineer's waiting. Leave out the rag-blockage boxes, that's the maintenance team's request.

Hi Grace, for the Berth 6 crane's spreader camera during daytime reefer handling, please find each damaged corner casting and mark its position with a box. My message on Tuesday flagged this as needing immediate turnaround, but the maintenance planner has since said it can simply follow the usual queue. A basic detection tier will do, nothing premium. The container-count report is for the yard planners and belongs to their own request.

Paint shop robot, line 3 night production: switch from counting bodies passing the arm to reading the VIN plate on each body. Cloud processing is fine; the cell PC doesn't need to do it. Basic accuracy works, no rush; the drip-defect boxes are the quality team's request.

re the cleanroom 2 gowning camera on the morning roster, I asked you to read the badge names, but scrap that, just let me know how many people walk through, a number is all I want. fine to process it in the cloud, it doesn't need to happen on the QA server. nothing fancy needed on accuracy, and the glove-breach boxes are the microbiology team's ask.

The Service shall transcribe the identification numbers displayed on firefighting aircraft passing the Mount Ash lookout during the declared fire season. The earlier draft of this schedule accepted entry-level recognition; following review by the Fire Controller, the most accurate recognition tier shall apply, as a misidentified aircraft cannot be tolerated. All imagery shall be analysed on the lookout's own equipment and shall not leave the tower. Smoke-plume localisation falls under the separate detection contract.

Headrig approach, sawmill infeed: locate each metal fragment embedded in incoming logs and box it in the frame. Detection tier raised from basic to maximum after last week's saw strike. Images stay on the mill's own server, nothing sent off-site; the board tally is for the dispatch office, not this system.

Hey, the tower inspection flight at turbine 22 this afternoon, I said count the bolts on the flange, but make it reading the torque markings stamped beside each bolt instead. Handle everything on the drone controller and don't push it to the cloud. The crack boxes are the blade inspector's job, not mine.

Hi Claire, for the lion enclosure camera during the overnight observation period, we'd like each animal located and marked with a box in every frame. I'd said earlier that footage had to go through the keeper office PC, but after checking with IT it no longer needs to happen there and you're welcome to use your cloud service. We need results by 8 tomorrow morning for the vet's check, so please treat it as a priority. The visitor headcount at the viewing deck is a different request from the education team and isn't needed here.

Penguin habitat, feeding session: the first request was to outline each bird in the frame; that's changed, we only need how many penguins are on the rocks, a single figure with no positions. Band-number reading is the keepers' own study, not this job.

question about the compactor bins along the esplanade over the weekend, can you count the overflow bags left beside each bin, just a number. I said do it on the bin controller, but council IT says their cloud's fine. make the count dead exact, it goes into the contractor penalty report, but no rush; the graffiti tag reading is the parks team's thing.

The Contractor is to locate each loose or missing bolt on the hanger clamps visible in images from the main-span inspection gantry during quarterly maintenance closures, returning a box delimiting each defect. This supersedes the original requirement to transcribe the clamp identification plates. Images shall be analysed using the bridge's own monitoring server and shall not be transmitted beyond the structure, and each analysis shall be completed ahead of all routine work while the lane closure remains in force. Counting of vehicle crossings is performed by the traffic authority and is excluded.

Vent fan bay, southbound bore: the job used to box each stalled fan in the frame; now it only reports how many fans are stopped. A basic read does the job, no need for the fine model. Signage reading at the portal is the traffic control centre's request.

Quick change for tonight's concert at the south stand turnstiles: I asked you to box every person coming through, but change it, just give me the number of entries. Crunch it on the stadium server, don't send it anywhere. A basic pass is fine and there's no hurry, and the ticket barcode reading is the box office's setup.

Hi Duncan, for the grading camera at the trimmer station on the night run, we need every knot and split on each board located and boxed within the image. My original request said entry-level accuracy would be acceptable, but the export customer has rejected two packs, so please move us to your most precise tier. All images must go through the mill's server and not to any outside service. We also need it running before tomorrow's first shipment, and the board-count reporting for the yard crew is a separate job.

Reefer van cargo cam, metro delivery route: switch from counting pallets to reading the batch codes on each carton label. Processing stays in the van's onboard unit, no uploads. Reads must be exact since they feed the recall log, but it isn't time-critical; the driver-presence boxes are the fleet safety team's request.

fyi, for the pole cams along Harbour Street at night, I'd asked for the shop signs to be read, but actually we need each e-scooter spotted and boxed on the footpath. cloud processing works, doesn't have to be done on the pole. basic accuracy does the job and there's no hurry; the pedestrian counts are the transport planners' thing.

The Service Provider shall read the numbers on the irrigation valve tags photographed by survey drones across the eastern orchard blocks during the pre-season audit and deliver them as text. The original scope required localisation of each valve with a bounding rectangle; that requirement is withdrawn. Reading accuracy shall be of the most exacting tier, results shall follow the ordinary delivery schedule without expediting, and imagery may be handled at the Provider's remote facilities rather than on the farm.
